findings.summary: Page 1 tells learners to never read non-public env vars in Client Components before it explains what a Client Component is or how env visibility works.
findings.evidence: "Never read non-public env vars in Client Components"

findings.summary: Page 1 ends with a stray unlabeled sentence block and a terse Q&A that poses questions with inline answers using inconsistent style, and the 'Generates?' answer is a run-together fragment.
findings.evidence: Generates? package.json, configs, starter app/; app/ routes, next.config builds
findings.fix: Rewrite as full short answers: 'Generates package.json, config files and a starter app/. app/ holds routes; next.config tunes the build.'

findings.summary: A bullet states a safety rule about env vars in the mental-model list before env vars are introduced, mixing a separate idea into the routing/config model.
findings.evidence: Never read non-public env vars in Client Components

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "localhost", "project").
findings.evidence: Run the new project with cd my-app && npm run dev; it serves on http://localhost:3000 by default
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The text claims a non-empty folder with conflicting files may be overwritten, but create-next-app aborts instead.
findings.evidence: A non-empty folder with conflicting files fails or overwrites.
findings.fix: Say that create-next-app lists the conflicting files and exits without writing anything, so the user must pick an empty folder or a new name.

findings.summary: The full-flags command is said to skip every prompt, but recent create-next-app versions still ask about options not covered by flags.
findings.evidence: Line 2 skips every prompt; --js replaces --ts
findings.fix: Say that the flags answer the prompts they cover. Add --turbopack or --webpack (and the React Compiler flag in newer versions), or pass --yes, to skip all prompts.

findings.summary: Code is shown before the idea behind it is stated: the long flag command appears with its explanation only after it.
findings.evidence:
npx create-next-app@latest my-app --ts --eslint --tailwind --src-dir --app --import-alias "@/*" --use-pnpm
Line 2 skips every prompt; --js replaces --ts
findings.fix: State 'Flags skip the prompts' first, then show the command.

findings.summary: Mistakes are written as prose sentences that hold several ideas instead of one-line bullets.
findings.evidence: Name must be lowercase and npm-safe. A non-empty folder with conflicting files fails or overwrites.
findings.fix: Split into two bullets: 'Name: lowercase, npm-safe' and 'Non-empty folder with conflicts: fails or overwrites'.

findings.summary: One bullet holds several ideas: prompt topics, default alias and installer flag are mixed across adjacent bullets.
findings.evidence: Covers TypeScript, ESLint, Tailwind, src/, App Router, alias (default @/*)
findings.fix: Keep the prompt list on one line and move the alias default to the flags/alias line.

findings.summary: Mistakes are prose and the group/private interview answer is garbled: '(group) is routed but hidden from the URL' conflicts with the table saying grouping only, and the term 'private' vs '_lib' is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: (group) is routed but hidden from the URL; _private is not routed
findings.fix: Say 'Group folders do not add a URL segment; routes inside them are still public. Underscore folders are not routed.' and use _private (or _lib) consistently.

findings.summary: Folder tree is described in bullets and a table rather than shown as a tree diagram, making the app/ structure harder to scan.
findings.evidence: app/ is the App Router root: each folder is a URL segment
findings.fix: Add a small file-tree diagram of app/ with layout.tsx, page.tsx, (shop)/, _lib/, blog/[slug]/ and the resulting URLs.

findings.summary: The Interview Point for this section is missing, so its three questions have no model answers.
findings.evidence: Page 4 ends with "Mistakes / Paths must match the real folders or imports break..." and has no interview block. The outline asks: "How does next.config.ts differ from tsconfig.json in responsibility? What does typedRoutes protect you from? How do you configure the @/* alias and why use it over relative imports?"
findings.fix: Add an Interview Point block. next.config configures framework behaviour and tsconfig configures types and aliases. typedRoutes rejects links to paths that do not exist. The @/* alias avoids ../../.. chains and survives file moves.

findings.summary: The tsconfig alias snippet and explanation omit the baseUrl-or-relative mapping caveat from the outline.
findings.evidence: The page shows only "paths": { "@/*": ["./src/*"] } and the label "tsconfig compilerOptions". It never says that paths works with a relative mapping or with baseUrl.
findings.fix: Add a line: paths entries are relative to tsconfig.json when baseUrl is not set, or relative to baseUrl when it is set.

findings.summary: Code block appears before its one-line idea, and the tsconfig snippet is split from the label that explains it.
findings.fix: State 'paths in tsconfig compilerOptions map @/* to ./src/*' before the snippet.

findings.summary: Bullets hold more than one idea, and the mistakes line is a two-sentence prose block.
findings.evidence: env, reactStrictMode | inline values, extra dev checks; Paths must match the real folders or imports break. Edit next.config without a restart and it looks like nothing changed.
findings.fix: Split env and reactStrictMode into separate table rows; split the mistakes into two bullets.

findings.summary: The Interview Point for ESLint and env variables is missing.
findings.evidence: Page 5 ends with "Remember / Read secrets only in server code." The outline asks: "What is the difference between a plain env variable and a NEXT_PUBLIC_ one? Which env file wins when the same key is in several? Why must NEXT_PUBLIC_ values be set before build?"
findings.fix: Add an Interview Point block answering the three questions: plain variables stay on the server, NEXT_PUBLIC_ values are inlined into the bundle; the priority order; inlining happens at build time, so a rebuild is needed.

findings.summary: Env priority table is stated as a numbered ranking but the surrounding bullets mix unrelated ideas, and the .env.local row folds three facts into one cell.
findings.evidence: 3 | .env.local | secrets, git-ignored, skipped in test
findings.fix: Keep the Use cell to one idea; move 'git-ignored' and 'skipped in test' into separate bullets.

findings.summary: Cheat sheet ends with a prose SSR leak paragraph and the env priority is a bare vertical list with winner/loser labels that is not clearly an ordered diagram.
findings.evidence: A plain variable in a Client Component still renders into the server HTML. Read secrets only in server code.
